title: Check and checkmate
intro: The whole game is about the king. Learn what check is, how to get out of it, and how checkmate wins the game.

lessons.title: What is check?
lessons.summary: Attack the king, and get your own king out of danger.

steps.title: Check and checkmate
steps.text: A short video will introduce this lesson here. For now, the coach walks you through it on the board.
When a piece attacks the king, the king is in check. Watch the rook slide up to attack the black king.
A king in check must escape at once. Here the black king can simply step forward, out of the rook's line.
Your turn: give check with the rook.
steps.hint: Rooks move in straight lines. Which line leads to the black king?
steps.ifWrong: That move does not attack the king. Look along the ranks and files.
steps.ifRight: Check! The rook attacks the king along the back row.

steps.text: Give check with the queen. There is more than one way!
steps.hint: The queen moves like a rook and a bishop together.
steps.ifWrong: The king is not attacked after that move. Try a straight line or a diagonal towards it.

steps.text: Your king is in check from the rook. Block the check with your bishop, on a square where it is safe.
steps.hint: Put the bishop between the rook and your king, next to your pawn.
steps.ifWrong: That gets out of check, but this time block it with the bishop.
steps.ifRight: Blocked! The bishop stands in the rook's way, and your pawn protects it.

feedback.c5e7: That blocks the check, but the rook simply takes your bishop. Block where your pawn protects it.
feedback.e1d1: Stepping aside escapes the check too. Here, practise blocking with the bishop.
feedback.e1f1: Stepping aside escapes the check too. Here, practise blocking with the bishop.
feedback.e1f2: Stepping aside escapes the check too. Here, practise blocking with the bishop.

lessons.title: Checkmate wins the game
lessons.summary: Check with no way out ends the game.

steps.text: Checkmate is a check the king cannot escape. The black king is shut in by its own pawns, so a check on the back row would be deadly.
The rook gives check. The king cannot move, nothing can block, and nothing can take the rook. That is checkmate, and White wins.

steps.hint: The black king is stuck on the back row, just like before.
steps.ifWrong: Not mate yet. Which square on the back row can the rook reach?
steps.ifRight: Checkmate! The back row was the king's weak spot.

steps.text: Checkmate in one move with the queen.
steps.hint: Your king already guards the squares in front of the black king.
steps.ifWrong: The king can still escape or it is not check. Look at the top row.

steps.hint: Same pattern as before: the back row.
steps.ifWrong: Not mate. Find a check the king cannot escape.

steps.text: Well done! Check means the king is attacked. Checkmate means it is attacked and has no escape, and that wins the game.
